utterances.text: I'm sorry, could I ask for a time frame since the previous question addressed 1991 and 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, perfectly legitimate. Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You talked about issuance of weapons to this commune. When did that occur? Can you give us a date?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall the date, the exact date when the mobilisation of the units took place. It was done then, whenever a unit was mobilised. It was done in that way. Mobilisation took place in accordance with the needs of control of the territory, and it could have been in spring of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. While we're on the subject of mobilisation, I want ask you in your capacity as secretary of the regional secretariat for National Defence, first of all, did you get paid a salary, separate and apart from that you received --

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Did you have a staff?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have a separate office where you could perform the functions of secretary of the regional secretariat?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Well, I began carrying out that function when I had more time. It was the period -- I think it was in June, second half of June. Then I used the office that already existed where people were already working before, the people from the unit which had been transformed, which had been transformed into this secretariat. The premises were located in the building of the former committee of the League of Communists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you told us you didn't have a staff when you were the secretary to the regional secretariat. Could you alone order a -- could you alone carry out or handle all the paperwork necessary for mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Well, my job before June, well, I did as much as I could.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Who was responsible for actually implementing the mobilisation? Did that happen on the republic level, municipal level? What level was responsible for actually getting the troops mobilised?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: The municipal level.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to clear up while we're talking about the secretariat for national defence, in your LiveNote testimony, in your testimony earlier today, page 57, line 24 -- excuse me, line 22, you were asked: "Who was your immediate supervisor? Who did you answer to?" And you said the following: "In terms of defence, in terms of how the jobs were carried Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. out, it would have been the republican defence minister. Within the organisation itself, the president of the ARK council, the executive council of Krajina." And I want to focus on that last sentence where you said: "Within the organisation itself, the president of the ARK council, the executive council of Krajina." What did you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Well, the executive council of ARK who was Nikola Erceg, it had its secretaries. The government was not fully composed, but it had its secretaries, and they had to -- responsible in terms of organisations towards the council. The mobilisation was linked exclusively to the Ministry of Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: What I'd like to do now with the Court's permission is to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session for a while, Madam Registrar, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever tell anyone before the arrival of the SOS that you had decided to block the streets of Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever tell anyone that that decision was made with members of the ARK Crisis Staff? Did you ever say that?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever tell anyone that was done with the consent and approval of General Talic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the -- your tasks as the secretary for the regional secretariat, when did those end?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Well, my duties stopped as early as in July. Actually, in July, the Minister of Defence Subotic ordered that the president of the executive council Nikola Erceg and I propose people who would be in charge of the department of National Defence in several parts of the region at the time. This was in early July. From the secretariat for defence of the region, several units were to be set up in the region. Petrovac, Drvar, Banja Luka, Doboj. And here, he actually assumed that this would be taken up by active officers and that there would be no secretariats in the ARK, but departments. And I understood this, that there would be a situation where they would be deprived of power. It was at the time that he asked us. I actually didn't propose any new people, nor Mr. Erceg, in the case of Banja Luka. Active-duty officers were appointed in Banja Luka. And I don't know about the other places.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We've talked about your role as commander of the Banja Luka TO. We've talked about your role as the secretary for the national secretariat. Let's now talk about the ARK Crisis Staff, because you told us that sometime in early May, you found out that you were appointed to the ARK Crisis Staff. If you want to, if you'd look at the exhibit in your notebook, 168, because I'm going to ask you some questions, and I'd like you to have that document in front of you in case you need to look at it. P168 is a decision on the formation of the war staff of the Autonomous Region of Krajina attributed to the president of the executive council, Mr. Erceg, dated 5 May 1992. How did you find out that you were selected, appointed to be a member of the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I found out after I had been called to come to that meeting.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your reaction once you had learned that you had been appointed to this entity?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I believe I already said that I wasn't particularly glad about this. This didn't make me happy. That's one thing. Secondly, it was by virtue of my position that when crisis staffs were established in the former state and then that I would be part of the crisis staff. Therefore, I didn't have a real say in whether I became member or not. One knew exactly under the legal procedure which persons would be appointed to crisis staffs as well as to National Defence Councils. That I have already talked about.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If we look at Prosecutor's Exhibit 168, page 2, we see you, Colonel Milorad Sajic, and then it says vice-president. When did you find out that you were the vice-president of the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I found out that that's what the decision had stated, that I became vice-president of the ARK Crisis Staff. But it was only later when I looked at the documents before giving my statement to the Office of the Prosecutor. That's where I saw it written for the first time. But I never was vice-president, and I never actually discharged this duty in actual fact, and I didn't feel that I was vice-president.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. If we look at this exhibit, P168, we see 1 through 15, 15 different named individuals. In 1992, in May when this document was issued, do you know whether the individuals listed 1 through 15 -- do you know which municipality they lived in?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: If it's the same document that I have before me, decision to set up crisis staff, is that the one you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: All these persons listed here, for the most part, are people from Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You say "for the most part." Can you tell us any one of those 15 people that came from outside Banja Luka, that resided outside Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: All of them resided in Banja Luka. I'm not sure about the pilot here, the major, who he was, but he did reside in Banja Luka. He had arrived in Banja Luka as an active military officer. They all did reside in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to talk to you about attendance at ARK meetings. When we met, I gave you a copy of Prosecutor's Exhibit 227, which is the ARK Gazette that covers a portion of the meetings held by the ARK Crisis Staff. Let me ask you: Did you have -- did you attend all the meetings of the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With your obligations to the TO as well as your obligations to the -- being the secretary, how many meetings of the ARK Crisis Staff do you believe that you attended?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I believe five or six. Thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't know if looking through Prosecutor's Exhibit 227 in your hotel room helped refresh your recollection, but can you generally tell us when your attendance at these meetings was? Was it May? Was it June? First part of July? What can you tell us, if anything, about when you attended the meetings?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Mostly it may have been May, June. I don't know that there were any meetings at all in July.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Recognising that you were there five, maybe six meetings, I'm going to ask you some questions about the attendance of other individuals. First of all, was Mr. Brdjanin present at every meeting you attended?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I'm going to do is rather than go down the list, I'm going to focus in first, and the list I'm talking about is Prosecutor's Number 168. If you need to have it there, get it in front of you. The first group of individuals that I want to talk to you about that are contained in the decision are the individuals that are in the military. So we would be talking first about number 8, General Talic. In the five, six meetings that you attended, did you ever see General Talic at the meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Once, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any of the meetings that you were there, was there ever any discussion about dealing with Mr. -- General Talic's absences from the crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know a Colonel Vojinovic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did he attend crisis staff meetings?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Several of them, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And do you know what -- why he did that? What purpose was he there for?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I think we even sat together at one or two meetings. He would usually listen to what was being said. He had no authority to present any of his ideas there, to accept or refuse. He just passed on the decisions and conclusions to his command. He was the assistant commander of the corps for civilian affairs. So usually he was there on behalf of the civilian affairs organ, but he did not have any powers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you ever remember any statements that Colonel Vojinovic may have made during crisis staff meetings about what he could or couldn't do?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I don't believe he spoke at meetings of the crisis staff. If there was anything he ever said, he would usually just say "I'll just write down what you've just said," but he never made any statements of his own. He never put forward any of his own positions because he was simply not authorised to do so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. During the five or six meetings that you attended, did the ARK Crisis Staff ever command General Talic or his representative to undertake any specific or certain acts?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: The crisis staff had no power to issue any orders to Talic. Maybe there was discussion about the situation in the military about problems, this may have been done at meetings, but certainly there were no official orders.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Let's talk now about the individual at number 9, Major Zoran Jokic. Do you know what branch of the military he was in?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I think he was a pilot in the air force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. You told us you were at five or six meetings. At those five or six meetings, did you ever see Colonel Jokic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Major, Major Jokic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I saw him -- I saw him once, and I asked who the man was because I hadn't known him. And I never saw him again after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. Same question with regard to General Talic and/or his representative. Did the ARK Crisis Staff ever command or direct Major Jokic to undertake a specific act?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to talk now about two individuals tied in with the police. Do you know who Stojan Zupljanin is?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He's the individual at number 10 on Exhibit P168. Do you remember seeing him at meetings of the ARK Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Perhaps once or twice. Not very often.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your understanding of what his position was in Banja Luka?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Stojan Zupljanin was the chief of the Security Services Centre, the regional centre, for Banja Luka which consisted of a number of municipalities. In simple terms, you'd say the police chief, the civilian police chief. His position was such that above him there was the minister of the interior, and he received orders, instructions, and decisions from the relevant minister. He was not associated with any other specific organ.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's look at the individual reflected at number 14, Slobodan Dubocanin. Do you know who he was?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I don't know what his name is doing here in this list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your understanding of his position, if any, in Banja Luka in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: He was a reserve officer. He was in the army. I don't know whether he left the army eventually or not. But I am not aware of any official position that he held.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With respect to his attendance, what can you tell us? How many times, if any, did you see him at an ARK Crisis Staff meeting?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: The same thing. Once, perhaps, the first time. I never noticed him again later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. With respect to Stojan Zupljanin, did the ARK Crisis Staff ever issue any direct orders to him as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: No. Not as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, let's go ahead and fill in the blanks by talking about the other individuals. Individual at number 3, Vojo Kupresanin, how would you characterise his attendance?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: He did attend some of the meetings. I'm not sure if we attended the same meetings, the two of us. But he did attend meetings, especially when the municipality presidents from the region attended because he was the president of the assembly of the Krajina region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. And we'll get to talking about the attendance of the municipality presidents in a bit. The name at number 4, Nikola Erceg, who is president of the executive council, do you remember him at the ARK Crisis Staff meetings that you attended?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I don't think he attended all the meetings. He was the president of the executive council, and he was there whenever problems to do with the economy, with supplies, staple goods to the population were being discussed. But I don't think those were official meetings. Those were work meetings. Those were no sessions of the crisis staff. As far as that was concerned, yes, he was there because the executive council was operating both in May and in June, and it was passing decisions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that -- you just mentioned work meetings. Did you attend these work meetings that you just mentioned?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: If you mean meetings with the presidents of the municipalities, yes, I did attend a number of those, but I do not know whether I attended all of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, no, no, what I was talking about was in your answer with respect to Mr. Erceg -- I see what you're talking about. And I'll come back to that. Let me go down to the next person on the list, number 5, Mr. Radic, the president of the municipality. How would you characterise his attendance?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: He came very rarely, if at all. I don't think he spoke at those meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what his attitude was towards the competence of the crisis staff?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: He did not see this body as a body that was above him, that was superior to him. He did not have any respect for this body as a superior body. He believed his duty as the president was to run the municipality and to rally behind him the republican organs in the exercise of his duties. And that was precisely how he acted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. The individual at number 6 is Radislav Vukic. What can you tell us about his attendance at these meetings?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Radislav Vukic, I can't say how many times he was there, but he was there. I don't think attendance was kept of who was there and who wasn't and how many times certain persons came. I can't say exactly how many times, but he was the party president and as such, yes, sometimes he did attend.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Number 7 is Dr. Milovan Milanovic. What about his attendance?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Very rarely, I think.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We skip 3 and go to number 11, Dr. Rajko Kuzmanovic. What can you tell us about his attendance?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I never saw him at any of the meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that Dr. Kuzmanovic was replaced by another individual whose name escapes me at the time, but he was the director of Banja Luka University? Do you remember that -- the replacement of Dr. Kuzmanovic?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Yes. There was a replacement in the rectorate of the university between Kuzmanovic and Mijanic, and he was later called upon to join. But he did not come very often to meetings of the crisis staff, Mijanic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You cleared that up. That takes us to number 12, Mr. Milan Puvacic. What was his attendance at crisis staff meetings like?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I only saw him very few times. Not that I attended all of the sessions myself, but Milan Puvacic was a secretary of sorts with the ARK council or another position perhaps. I don't know really. I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I just say for the record, Mr. Brdjanin is shaking his head in response to some of the questions asked by counsel and nodding to others. I just noticed that. I'd ask that he not do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's a good thing the witness hasn't been looking at Mr. Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's how I noticed it, because I saw the witness looking over at Mr. Brdjanin shaking his head, and I wanted to bring Your Honours' attention to that fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman, I will let Mr. Cunningham concentrate on the questions, and you look after the rest, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We're almost done, Mr. Sajic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I didn't hear you say thank you, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: "Thank you, Mr. Ackerman."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cunningham.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, we're now down to number 13, who is Jovo Rosic. Tell us about his attendance? Tell us how many times you remember seeing him while you were there?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: Jovo Rosic, he's from the Justice Department. He was later with the Ministry of Republika Srpska, I believe. But he did not come to those meetings, the meetings of the crisis staff, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last person I'm going to ask you about is number 15, Nenad Stevanovic -- it says Stevanovic?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Nenad Stevandic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: That's what I assumed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nenad Stevandic, do you remember seeing him at any of the meetings you attended?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I did see him once or twice I believe, the first two possibly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My last question of the day because it's about time to break: Of these people who missed meetings including yourself, were they ever sanctioned for punished for their failure to attend these meetings?

utterances.speaker: MILORAD SAJIC
utterances.text: I was never admonished myself, or sanctioned, and I don't believe that they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: It's a perfect stopping point, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Sajic, we are going to stop here for today. We will continue tomorrow. Between now and tomorrow, you're not to contact anyone with regard to your testimony here. You're not to discuss it with anyone, irrespective of whether you approach other people or whether you are approached. So you are still testifying here, and you're not allowed to discuss your testimony. Is that clear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very much so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. You'll be escorted now by Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We will continue tomorrow in the afternoon, by the way.

utterances.speaker: MR. CUNNINGHAM
utterances.text: I think it's consistent with what we've talked about before. He can leave the exhibit book in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, you can leave that here. Mr. Cunningham will look after it. Thank you, good afternoon. See you tomorrow in the afternoon. Anything else before we rise? Nothing.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, what I propose to do, I hope, is some -- send a list of the potential sites to Mr. Ackerman by email this afternoon, and then perhaps we can reach an agreed --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can come back to us as soon as possible. And then the other thing I wanted to mention is that Registrar has recommended to me, to us, not to think about going there in January or February because of the weather. So that has been made quite clear. I don't know --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We've all been there, Your Honour. It depends. It's better, probably preferable, to go in March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. So keep that in mind, please. Thank you, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 16th day of December, 2003, at 2.15 p.m. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
